newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Washington Post page one - Jan 1.

text.p: The Washington Post carried the following stories on its front page on January 1:

WASHINGTON - D.C. Mayor Marion Barry vowed to fight "to the death" for funding for the University of the District of Columbia and alleged that the school has been targeted for $16 million in cuts because "some people don't want blacks and young blacks to get a quality education."

WASHINGTON - For the last 24 years, Cedar Hill, the stately white brick mansion in Anacostia where Frederick Douglass lived the last two decades of his life, has been open to the public free of charge, but now is among the sites where the Park Service plans to impose fees.
WASHINGTON - The Clinton Administration announced controversial new restrictions on tourist flights over Grand Canyon National Pak.
WASHINGTON - The Dow Jones industrial average ended the year with a gain of 26 percent, an especially impressive run following the blue chip measure's 33 percent rise in 1995.
WASHINGTON - Major cities across the nation experienced sharply fewer homicides in 1996, hitting a 30-year low in some cases and driving an overall drop in violent crime that began five years ago.

BEIJING - As China and other developing nations join the global economy, new tensions are rising among many who remain dissatisfied, buffeted by modernization, jealous of others' greater fortune and fearful they will be turned aside and pushed back into poverty.
